scope: Targeted scoping review begun 19 October 2026 and supplemented 23 October 2026, not an exhaustive systematic review. Abstract-level limits are disclosed.

scientific.authors: D. Anggraini, K. Adi and J. E. Suseno
scientific.title: Electronic document management systems implementation across industries systematic analysis
scientific.venue: Indonesian Journal of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science 36(1), 264–273
scientific.finding: Adoption depends on technical, individual and organisational factors as well as trust.
scientific.limitation: Heterogeneous sectors cannot establish the needs of the proposed department.
scientific.project_use: Compare adoption themes with the Astana interview notes and test the complete review journey with pilot users.

scientific.authors: A. Anas and T. A. Salim
scientific.title: Tinjauan literatur sistematis pemanfaatan electronic document management system bagi organisasi dalam menunjang manajemen pengetahuan
scientific.method: Review of ten EDMS studies from 2015–2020
scientific.finding: Document storage, distribution and security support knowledge work alongside capable staff.
scientific.limitation: Two databases and an older evidence window restrict coverage.
scientific.project_use: Use searchable metadata and onboarding tasks rather than treating storage alone as success.

scientific.title: The Role of Business Process Management in Digital Innovation and Digital Transformation: A Systematic Literature Review
scientific.access: Publisher abstract and author manuscript identification
scientific.finding: Process management and digital transformation interact at organisational and technical levels.
scientific.limitation: Broad BPM findings do not prove a particular document approval design will help.
scientific.project_use: Model the existing and proposed process and evaluate task time against a baseline.

scientific.authors: A. K. Y. S. Mohamed, D. Auer, D. Hofer and J. Küng
scientific.title: A systematic literature review for authorization and access control definitions strategies and models
scientific.venue: International Journal of Web Information Systems 18(2/3), 156–180
scientific.finding: Policy models and enforcement mechanisms need distinct definitions.
scientific.limitation: A classification cannot establish that one implementation enforces its policy.
scientific.project_use: Specify role plus ownership checks and test direct access to each protected resource.

scientific.authors: B. Q. Truong, A. Nguyen-Duc and N. T. C. Van
scientific.title: A Quantitative Review of the Research on Business Process Management in Digital Transformation A Bibliometric Approach
scientific.finding: BPM and transformation form a broad growing research field.
scientific.limitation: Citation networks describe research attention rather than measured organisational benefit.
scientific.project_use: Keep the project contribution narrow and evaluate observable workflow outcomes.

scientific.authors: F. Milani, K. Kubrak and J. Nava
scientific.title: Strategic redesign of business processes in the digital age A framework
scientific.method: Review of 40 process redesign case studies
scientific.finding: Capabilities can inform process redesign beyond replacing existing technology.
scientific.limitation: Cross-case mappings need local validation and do not predict our effect size.
scientific.project_use: Use explicit ownership, a frozen review version and visible next action as redesign hypotheses.

scientific.authors: R. S. Sandhu, E. J. Coyne, H. L. Feinstein and C. E. Youman
scientific.title: Role Based Access Control Models
scientific.finding: Permissions attach to roles and users receive role memberships.
scientific.limitation: Basic role membership alone cannot express every document relationship.
scientific.project_use: Combine a small role set with ownership and assignment predicates. Retained as a foundation.

scientific.authors: W. M. P. van der Aalst
scientific.title: The Application of Petri Nets to Workflow Management
scientific.venue: Journal of Circuits Systems and Computers 8(1), 21–66
scientific.access: Author paper and academic bibliographic record
scientific.finding: Explicit process logic supports reasoning about valid progress and termination.
scientific.limitation: The proposed finite-state workflow is simpler and has not undergone a Petri-net proof.
scientific.project_use: Enumerate transitions and test invalid paths and completion. Retained as a foundation.

scientific.title: Challenges in the technological adoption of document management systems
scientific.method: Cross-sectional correlational survey of 998 public-sector DMS workers
scientific.finding: Performance expectancy, effort expectancy and social influence correlate with intention to use a DMS.
scientific.limitation: Non-probability public-sector sample and correlational design do not establish causality or target-organisation needs.
scientific.project_use: Include ease of use, onboarding and role clarity in prototype feedback without promising an adoption rate.

scientific.authors: R. Nurbatyrova, B. Japarov, N. Apakhayev, B. Abdulaziz and S. Khushkeldiyeva
scientific.title: Digital Transformation of Archives in the Context of the Introduction of an Electronic Document Management System in Kazakhstan
scientific.access: Publisher abstract and Crossref citation record
scientific.method: Theoretical investigation of archive digitisation and EDMS context in Kazakhstan
scientific.finding: Describes national archival and document-management context.
scientific.limitation: State-archive focus cannot establish departmental workflow needs or current legal compliance.
scientific.project_use: Compare local terminology with the interview notes and validate archival expectations and pilot scope with the supervisor.
